name: Charcot Neuroarthropathy of the Foot
definition: Progressive destructive arthropathy of the foot or ankle occurring in severe peripheral neuropathy, most often associated with diabetes, with risk of deformity, ulceration and amputation.

typical: Warm swollen foot with relatively little pain
Midfoot collapse or rocker-bottom deformity in later disease

redFlags.item: Any red hot swollen neuropathic foot requires urgent assessment

investigations.principle: Early diagnosis is critical and imaging must be interpreted with infection risk.
investigations.MRI: MRI is useful for early Charcot change and for assessing osteomyelitis differential; CT helps bony architecture.
investigations.radiographs: Weight-bearing radiographs may be normal early and later show fragmentation/subluxation.

green: Immediate off-loading/immobilization when active Charcot is suspected
Optimize diabetes, footwear and ulcer prevention
amber: Do not encourage weight-bearing exercise during active Charcot; surgery is selected for severe unstable deformity or recurrent ulceration.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Madhumeha-associated Pada/Asthi-Sandhi pathology may be documented only in parallel; modern off-loading and infection exclusion are essential.

patientEducation.summary: Progressive destructive arthropathy of the foot or ankle occurring in severe peripheral neuropathy, most often associated with diabetes, with risk of deformity, ulceration and amputation.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
